title: aos-seat.v1
description: AOS seat manifest. Describes one agent seat: identity, plane routing, behavior tags, capability grants, tier ladder, prompt buffers, bus interfaces, surfaces, hosts, and toolsets. Seat fields may be embedded in a larger harness profile document; unknown top-level keys are therefore allowed (harness-owned fields), while tier entries are closed except for x_-prefixed extensions. The tiers array is an ordered ladder; launcher flags may select a rung, never redefine it.

name.description: Stable seat name (matches the harness profile name).

node_type.description: Role of this node in the delegation graph.

behavior.description: Behavior tags carried by the seat manifest (e.g. orchestrate).

lane.description: Lane label within the plane (free-form, e.g. a project lane).

capabilities.description: Granted capabilities (e.g. read, job.enqueue, buffer.apply, review, escalate, graph.own).

tiers.description: Ordered model ladder. Each entry is one rung; order in the array is the ladder order.

rung.description: Ladder rung: primary, fallback, or candidate.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this rung; null means harness default.

buffers.description: Prefill prompt buffers applied to this seat's prompts.

interfaces.description: Bus interfaces used by the seat.

surfaces.description: Surfaces this seat is reachable on (e.g. tui, cli).

hosts.description: Hosts this seat may run on (tmux-connect registry names).

toolsets.description: Granted toolsets. Exact orchestrate behavior permits only the explicitly supported names below; wildcard, composite, and unknown aliases require separate characterization before they can be granted.

terminal.description: Deny-by-default policy for orchestration terminal grants. Only these fully anchored read/validation commands are characterized; no arbitrary regex, shell, or command prefix is accepted. Harness approval must enforce this policy before ordinary/container approvals; seat check validates the manifest only. Extend this catalog only after independent command review.
